The line \(\ell_t\) is given by \(x+t y+z=0\).

\[

\]

\[
(-t y-1)^{3}+y^{3}+1=0
\]
\[
\Longrightarrow\;(1-t^{3})y^{3}-3t^{2}y^{2}-3t y=0
\]
\[
\Longrightarrow\;y\big[(1-t^{3})y^{2}-3t^{2}y-3t\big]=0 .
\]

Thus the intersection consists of the point \(y=0\) (which always lies on both \(D\) and \(\ell_t\)) and the two roots of the quadratic  

\[
Q(y)=(1-t^{3})y^{2}-3t^{2}y-3t .
\]

\[
\Delta = ( -3t^{2})^{2}-4(1-t^{3})(-3t)=9t^{4}+12t-12t^{4}=12t-3t^{4}=0 .
\]

Hence  

\[
3t\bigl(4-t^{3}\bigr)=0\quad\Longrightarrow\quad t=0\ \text{or}\ t^{3}=4 .
\]

The non‑trivial real solution is  

\[
t=4^{1/3}\approx 1.587401051\;.

\boxed{1.5874}
